description: We have a team consisting of Birce Doğan, Arya Ergin, Lara Sıla Taşdemir, and Çınar Karali, all students at Ted İzmir College. We chose the challenge of designing a space mission game. Our game is named Orbit Odyssey. In this game, we earn points by completing space missions, and we use these points to upgrade our suit, spacecraft, and features. By designing a game that is both fun and educational, we aim to make it enjoyable for players to learn about space and space physics while having fun.
summary: As Team Space Smyrna, we developed an interactive educational game for the 2026 Space Mission Design Game challenge to teach students how to plan and conduct a space mission in a fun, engaging way. For students who rarely get to experiment with an entire mission from concept to operation, real-world aerospace trade-offs often feel abstract. Our project directly addresses this challenge by letting players of all ages configure missions, manage limited resources, and make strategic decisions while discovering how essential space technologies work. By turning complex constraints into hands-on gameplay, players see firsthand how each choice shapes mission success. This experience is important because it builds critical problem-solving skills and inspires the next generation of explorers. Ultimately, our game makes STEM learning accessible, promotes space exploration, and sparks curiosity by bringing real space missions to life.
details:
ORBITAL ODYSSEY

Project Details

Team Name: Team Space Smyrna
Challenge: Space Mission Design Game
NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026

1. Project Overview

As Team Space Smyrna, we developed Orbital Odyssey, a 3D interactive space exploration and physics learning game for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge. Our project was created in response to the challenge of making space mission design more accessible, understandable, and engaging through an interactive digital experience. By combining mission-based gameplay, astronaut customization, planetary exploration, scientific questions, and physics-related challenges, we aim to introduce players to the exciting world of space exploration while encouraging them to learn through participation.

Space missions involve much more than travelling from one place to another. Every mission requires a purpose, careful preparation, suitable equipment, and decisions based on scientific and technical considerations. Mission teams must understand their destinations, consider possible routes, and determine how to achieve their objectives. These processes involve different areas of science and engineering that are often difficult to understand when presented only through theoretical explanations.

Orbital Odyssey transforms these ideas into a game environment in which players can become active participants in a space mission. Players begin by creating and customizing their astronaut, receive assignments from a scientist character, explore different routes and orbits, and complete activities during their missions. The game also includes educational questions at different difficulty levels, allowing players to test their knowledge while progressing through the experience.

Our main intention is to bring together education and entertainment without separating scientific learning from gameplay. We want players to experience the feeling of being part of a mission while discovering concepts related to physics, space exploration, and scientific investigation. Through this approach, Orbital Odyssey aims to make STEM learning more interactive and inspire greater curiosity about the universe.

2. Background and Problem Statement

Space exploration is one of the most complex fields of modern science and technology. A successful space mission depends on the coordination of many different elements, including mission objectives, spacecraft systems, scientific instruments, orbital paths, communication, and resource limitations. These elements are connected, meaning that a decision made during one stage of a mission can affect other stages as well.

For students and people who are interested in space, understanding these relationships can be challenging. Textbooks and traditional educational materials provide important scientific information, but they do not always allow learners to experience how different mission decisions work together. Reading about a spacecraft's journey, for example, is different from participating in a simulated journey and completing mission objectives.

We identified this gap between theoretical knowledge and interactive experience as an important educational problem. Many people are fascinated by planets, astronauts, and spacecraft, but the planning and scientific reasoning behind real missions may remain unfamiliar to them. We wanted to create a project that could make these processes easier to approach.

Another important aspect of the challenge is that space mission design requires both scientific knowledge and decision-making. A mission is not simply a sequence of unrelated activities. Its objectives, route, and operational requirements must be considered together. We wanted to communicate this interconnected structure through a game that gives players clear goals and opportunities to interact with the environment.

Orbital Odyssey addresses this problem by introducing space exploration through a structured and interactive experience. Rather than presenting scientific information only as text, the game encourages players to explore, respond to assignments, complete activities, and answer questions. In this way, the project aims to make scientific concepts more approachable and memorable.

3. Project Purpose and Motivation

Our primary motivation was to make learning about space more engaging and accessible, especially for students and young people. Space exploration has the potential to inspire curiosity about science, technology, engineering, and mathematics. However, the technical processes behind real missions can sometimes feel distant from everyday learning experiences.

We wanted to create a game in which players could take an active role in a space exploration journey. Instead of simply observing planets or reading facts about astronauts, players would be able to customize an astronaut, receive a mission, explore a destination, and complete tasks. This creates a connection between the player and the scientific environment.

Another important purpose of the project is to encourage curiosity through exploration. We believe that learning becomes more meaningful when people are encouraged to ask questions and discover information themselves. By combining mission assignments with planetary activities and educational questions, we aim to create opportunities for players to think about the science behind their actions.

We also wanted the game to be suitable for players with different levels of knowledge. Not everyone has the same background in physics or astronomy. The inclusion of questions at different difficulty levels helps provide a range of educational challenges and allows players to engage with scientific topics at different levels.

Ultimately, our motivation is to show that space science does not have to be limited to complex technical explanations. It can also be introduced through creative, interactive, and enjoyable experiences that encourage people to explore further.

4. Game Concept and Overall Gameplay

Orbital Odyssey is designed as a 3D space mission and physics exploration experience. Its gameplay follows a mission-based structure in which players progress through different stages of a space exploration journey.

The experience begins with astronaut customization. Players can personalize their character using the available visual options, creating an astronaut who represents them within the game. This stage introduces the player to the environment and establishes their role in the upcoming mission.

After customization, players enter the mission process. A scientist character assigns missions and introduces the objectives that players are expected to complete. This character provides a narrative connection between the player and the scientific purpose of the mission.

Players then progress through the available mission stages, which include different routes and orbits. These elements introduce the idea that space exploration involves considering the journey as well as the destination. Players continue through the mission and encounter information and activities related to space.

At the destination, players can participate in interactive exploration tasks, including activities such as sample collection. These tasks represent the investigative side of scientific exploration and give players objectives beyond simply reaching a location.

Educational questions are also integrated into the gameplay. The questions have different difficulty levels and allow players to test their understanding of scientific concepts. At the end of the mission, a results and scoring system provides an evaluation of the player's performance.

This structure connects several parts of a space mission experience: preparing an astronaut, receiving an assignment, travelling, exploring, completing tasks, answering questions, and evaluating the results.

Controls: WASD keys to move (In the spacecraft W key is for going up and S key is for going down), also can move with arrow keys (↑←↓→), Space button for jetpack, Shift button for going faster, F key for collecting samples, E key to complete mission (You should be near your spacecraft), hold left mouse button to move the crosshair.

5. Astronaut Customization

Astronaut customization is one of the first interactive elements players encounter in Orbital Odyssey. Before beginning their mission, players can personalize their astronaut through the visual customization options available in the game.

The astronaut represents the player throughout the exploration experience. We included customization to give players a more personal connection to the game world and allow them to create a character that reflects their preferences.

The visual elements of an astronaut also help establish the game's identity. Spacesuits, helmets, and other astronaut-related details are strongly associated with space exploration. Including these elements makes the setting recognizable and helps players feel that they are preparing for a space mission.

Although customization is primarily a visual feature, it contributes to player engagement. It gives players an opportunity to interact with the game before beginning the mission itself and creates a sense of participation from the very beginning.

We wanted the experience to feel like the player is entering a role rather than simply controlling an object on the screen. The astronaut becomes the player's representation within the fictional mission environment.

6. Scientist Character and Mission Assignment System

An important part of Orbital Odyssey is the scientist character who assigns missions to the player. This character introduces the objectives and gives the player a clear reason to explore the game environment.

We included a scientist character because scientific exploration is based on questions, research objectives, and planned activities. In real space missions, scientists and mission teams work together to determine what needs to be investigated and what information should be collected.

The scientist character represents this research-oriented side of space exploration. Through mission assignments, players are introduced to the idea that every exploration activity should have a purpose.

The mission system also provides structure to the gameplay. Instead of exploring without direction, players receive objectives that guide their progress. This makes the experience easier to follow and helps connect different activities into a larger mission.

We wanted the player to understand that reaching a destination is only one part of a mission. The objectives assigned before and during exploration are equally important because they determine what the mission is intended to achieve.

By introducing missions through a character, we also create a more understandable narrative framework. The player receives guidance, learns what is expected, and then takes part in completing the assigned activities.

7. Routes and Orbits

Orbital Odyssey includes different routes and orbits as part of its space exploration experience. These elements help introduce players to the idea that the journey through space is an important part of mission planning.

In real space exploration, a spacecraft cannot simply move to any destination without considering the path it must follow. Orbital mechanics and trajectory planning are important parts of understanding how spacecraft travel through space.

We wanted to introduce this concept in an accessible way through the game's exploration structure. Different routes and orbits provide variety and help communicate that the path selected for a mission is an important consideration.

These elements also support the educational purpose of the game. They create opportunities to introduce players to the relationship between space travel, physics, and mission planning.

Rather than treating space as an empty environment in which movement has no constraints, Orbital Odyssey aims to introduce the idea that missions take place within a physical environment governed by scientific principles.

8. Planetary Exploration and Sample Collection

Planetary exploration is one of the central activities in Orbital Odyssey. After progressing through the mission, players reach their destination and participate in interactive activities within the exploration environment.

One of these activities is sample collection. This feature introduces players to the idea that scientific missions often involve gathering material and information for further investigation.

Sample collection is important in the context of planetary science because studying materials from another environment can help scientists investigate its characteristics and history. In a simplified game environment, this activity provides a way to represent the investigative purpose of space exploration.

We included interactive tasks to make exploration more meaningful. Instead of simply viewing a planet, players are encouraged to engage with the environment and complete objectives.

These activities also help create a sense of progression. Players move from preparing for the mission to travelling and then conducting exploration tasks. This sequence helps communicate that a space mission consists of multiple stages, each with its own purpose.

Through planetary exploration, we aim to encourage players to think about what scientists might investigate when exploring another world and why collecting information is an important part of scientific research.

9. Physics Learning and Educational Questions

Physics is closely connected to space exploration. The movement of spacecraft, the behaviour of objects in space, and the conditions involved in travelling between celestial bodies can all be understood through physical principles.

For this reason, Orbital Odyssey includes educational questions related to scientific knowledge, including physics-related topics. We wanted to make learning part of the gameplay rather than presenting it as a completely separate activity.

The game features questions at different difficulty levels. This allows the educational challenges to cover different levels of knowledge and gives players opportunities to test what they know.

Different difficulty levels are important because players may have different levels of familiarity with physics and astronomy. By offering questions at varying levels, we aim to make the experience more inclusive and provide opportunities for players to challenge themselves.

The questions also encourage active participation. Players are not only observing the environment; they are asked to think, recall information, and apply their knowledge.

We believe that this combination of exploration and questions can make scientific learning more engaging. When a question appears within the context of a mission, it becomes part of the player's overall experience rather than an isolated exercise.

10. Scoring and Mission Results

The results and scoring system provides an evaluation of the player's performance at the end of the mission. It gives players a clear overview of their progress and creates a sense of completion.

The scoring experience connects mission activities with the player's performance. Mission achievements and gameplay elements contribute to the final evaluation, while time-related bonuses may also be included where applicable.

We wanted to include a results screen because feedback is an important part of an interactive learning experience. Players should be able to see that their actions and decisions have contributed to the outcome of the mission.

The results screen also provides a natural ending to the mission. After completing exploration tasks and educational challenges, players receive an evaluation that marks the conclusion of their experience.

By combining mission completion and educational questions, the scoring system helps connect the game's entertainment elements with its learning objectives.

11. Artificial Intelligence Usage

During the development of Orbital Odyssey, we used Google Gemini as an AI-assisted tool. Gemini supported several stages of our development process, including coding, voice generation, information gathering, and design.

Coding Assistance

Developing an interactive game involves technical planning, implementation, and problem-solving. We used Gemini as a supporting resource during the coding process. It helped us work through development-related questions and supported our efforts to organize and implement parts of the project.

AI assistance was particularly useful as a tool for exploring possible approaches and supporting our workflow. However, the overall project concept, development decisions, and integration of the game's elements remained part of our team's work.

Voice Generation

Audio can contribute significantly to the atmosphere and communication of an interactive game. Since Orbital Odyssey includes a scientist character and mission assignments, voice content can help support the player's understanding of the experience.

We used Gemini during the voice generation stage as part of our work on the game's audio elements. This supported our efforts to make the experience more engaging and to connect the player with the mission environment.

Information Gathering

Research was another important part of the development process. Since our game focuses on space exploration and physics, we needed to collect and organize relevant information.

We used Gemini as an assisting tool during information gathering. It helped us explore relevant topics and organize information that could support the research and development process.

Design Support

Gemini also supported the design stage. Designing an educational game requires balancing visual presentation, gameplay, and scientific content. We used AI assistance while developing and organizing ideas related to the project.

Overall, we used artificial intelligence as a supporting tool in selected stages of development. Our intention was to improve our workflow and make the development process more efficient while maintaining our team's creative and technical contribution.

12. NASA Data Sources and Scientific Research

Scientific reliability was an important consideration throughout the development of Orbital Odyssey. Since the project focuses on space exploration and mission-related concepts, we wanted our research to be informed by reliable scientific resources.

For this reason, we benefited from NASA-related data and resources. The resources we referred to included:

  • GMAT
  • MDL
  • Design and Develop Science Mission
  • Orrery with Potentially Hazardous Asteroids

We selected these resources because we wanted to support our research with information connected to NASA's scientific and educational work.

Our use of these resources was part of our effort to understand space mission concepts and inform the scientific aspects of the game. We wanted to avoid relying entirely on assumptions when developing a project about a scientific subject.

The resources also helped us approach the project with a stronger focus on scientific reliability. Since Orbital Odyssey is intended to introduce players to space exploration, it was important for us to consider the accuracy of the information behind the experience.

We believe that educational games should make scientific information accessible without presenting unsupported claims as facts. By referring to NASA-related resources, we aimed to create a stronger connection between the game's interactive content and real scientific knowledge.

13. Technology and Development Approach

Orbital Odyssey was developed as a 3D interactive experience. Its design brings together visual elements, character interaction, mission progression, exploration activities, and educational content.

Creating this type of game requires attention to both the technical and creative aspects of development. The game needs to provide a clear experience for players while also communicating the intended educational ideas.

Our development approach focused on connecting the different elements into one mission-based experience. Character customization introduces the player, the scientist character provides objectives, routes and orbits contribute to the exploration process, and interactive tasks give players activities to complete.

Educational questions and the scoring system then connect the gameplay with the learning objectives. In this way, the different features contribute to the same overall purpose rather than functioning as unrelated elements.

We also used Google Gemini to support coding, voice generation, research, and design. This allowed us to use AI assistance as one of the tools within our development workflow.

14. Educational Impact and STEM Learning

One of the main goals of Orbital Odyssey is to make STEM learning more engaging. STEM brings together science, technology, engineering, and mathematics, all of which are important to modern space exploration.

Space missions provide a natural context for introducing these subjects. Physics helps explain movement and orbital behaviour, engineering contributes to spacecraft design, and scientific research helps determine what missions should investigate.

Through its different gameplay elements, Orbital Odyssey aims to introduce players to this interconnected nature of space exploration.

The routes and orbits help introduce mission-related concepts. Planetary exploration and sample collection communicate the importance of observation and investigation. Educational questions encourage players to think about scientific topics and test their knowledge.

The mission assignment system also introduces the importance of objectives and planning. Players are given tasks and must understand what they are expected to achieve.

We hope these elements will encourage players to become more interested in science and recognize that scientific exploration involves curiosity, research, problem-solving, and careful decision-making.

15. Accessibility and Engagement

We wanted Orbital Odyssey to be an experience that could attract players who have different levels of scientific knowledge. Not every player is already familiar with orbital mechanics, physics, or planetary science.

For this reason, we aimed to present scientific ideas through an interactive environment rather than relying only on complex explanations. Players can begin by engaging with the astronaut and mission experience, then encounter scientific concepts through exploration and questions.

The different question difficulty levels also contribute to this goal. They provide a way to introduce a range of challenges and allow players to engage with educational content at different levels.

The visual nature of a 3D environment can also help make the subject more approachable. Space exploration is a topic that naturally encourages imagination, and an interactive environment gives players an opportunity to engage with that interest.

Our goal is to make the learning experience feel like part of the adventure. We want players to become curious about the scientific ideas behind the game and feel encouraged to explore those ideas further.

16. Challenges and Development Considerations

Developing an educational space exploration game involves balancing several different goals. The game should be interesting to play, but it should also communicate scientific ideas clearly and responsibly.

One of the main considerations was finding a balance between gameplay and education. We wanted the game to provide a sense of exploration and progression without losing its educational purpose.

Another consideration was organizing the experience into understandable stages. Mission assignments, routes, exploration tasks, questions, and results need to work together so that players can understand their progress.

Scientific reliability was also an important consideration. Since the project is connected to space exploration, we wanted to use credible resources during research and avoid presenting unsupported information as established scientific fact.

We used AI assistance and NASA-related resources to support different parts of the process. These tools and resources helped us approach the project from both a technical and research-oriented perspective.

17. Future Development Potential

Orbital Odyssey provides a foundation for further development. Space exploration includes a wide range of scientific topics and mission types, which creates opportunities to expand the game's content over time.

Future versions could include additional mission scenarios, more planetary destinations, and a wider variety of scientific exploration activities. The educational question system could also be expanded to cover more topics and provide additional levels of challenge.

Further development could also introduce more detailed explanations of the scientific concepts represented in the game. This could help players connect their in-game experiences with real scientific research and space exploration.

Additional mission-planning elements could provide further opportunities to explore the decisions involved in real missions. These improvements would help expand the educational scope of the project while maintaining its interactive nature.

These ideas represent possible future directions rather than features that we claim are already fully implemented. Our current work establishes a starting point for continued development and improvement.

19. Conclusion

As Team Space Smyrna, we created Orbital Odyssey with the goal of making space exploration more accessible, interactive, and educational. We wanted to transform the complex ideas behind space missions into an experience in which players could take part in exploration, complete objectives, and discover scientific concepts.

Through astronaut customization, scientist-assigned missions, different routes and orbits, planetary exploration, sample collection, physics-related questions, and mission results, we aimed to create a connected space exploration experience.

We used Google Gemini to support coding, voice generation, information gathering, and design during development. We also referred to NASA-related resources, including GMAT, MDL, Design and Develop Science Mission, and Orrery with Potentially Hazardous Asteroids, to support our research and focus on scientific reliability.

Our project reflects our belief that education can become more engaging when scientific concepts are connected to interactive experiences. We hope Orbital Odyssey will encourage curiosity, introduce players to the ideas behind space missions, strengthen their interest in STEM, and inspire them to learn more about the universe.
